situation: Series A pitch to three VC partners in San Francisco. Our startup sells inventory forecasting software to independent cafes: 35k dollars in monthly revenue and 120 paying customers.

scenario.title: Series A Pitch: Cafe Forecasting Bet
scenario.setting: Late-morning partner meeting in a glass conference room at a mid-size VC firm in SoMa, San Francisco. Deck on screen, three partners across the table, 20 minutes on the clock.
scenario.user_role: Founder of a startup selling inventory forecasting software to independent cafes, pitching for Series A.
scenario.user_goal: Convince the three partners the business can be venture-scale and secure a concrete next step toward investment.
user_knows: There are 120 paying customers who are independent cafes
The product is inventory forecasting software
This is a Series A pitch to three VC partners in San Francisco

cast.name: Sarah Klein
cast.appearance: Mid-40s, dark blazer, short brown hair, MacBook open
cast.voice: Direct, fast-paced, cuts in with math questions
cast.goal: Test if independent cafes can ever support a venture-scale outcome and push the founder toward multi-location or enterprise
cast.secret: The firm lost $2.1M on a single-location restaurant SaaS last year and now requires over 110% net revenue retention for any SMB food deal
cast.reveal_when: asks what specific proof or metrics would make a cafe SMB bet fundable for their firm
red_lines: will not give a valuation or term sheet in the room
will not accept TAM based on cafe count without revenue math
cast.history: She first met the founder six weeks ago after his 5-minute pitch at the SaaS Seed Showcase, where she pressed him on cafe TAM. Her last exchange was an email inviting him to this partner meeting and telling him to bring market math that proves venture scale.

cast.name: Marcus Webb
cast.appearance: Late-30s Black man, light button-down with sleeves rolled, notebook
cast.voice: Calm, analytical, presses on churn and acquisition cost
cast.goal: Expose weakness in retention and sales efficiency and force the founder to prove sticky, efficient growth
cast.secret: Spoke last week with two ex-customers who said onboarding took 3+ weeks and that is why they quit
cast.reveal_when: asks directly what negative feedback or churn reasons they have heard about the product
red_lines: will not be swayed by logos or anecdotes without numbers
will not drop churn if the founder deflects
cast.history: He joined a 30-minute follow-up Zoom last week where the founder walked him through early retention cohorts and CAC. His last exchange was asking the founder to bring a churn breakdown by cafe size and acquisition cost to today's meeting.

cast.name: David Park
cast.appearance: Early-40s Asian man, gray sweater, leans back with coffee
cast.voice: Friendly but probing, asks about distribution and focus
cast.goal: Push the founder to show a scalable way to acquire hundreds more cafes beyond founder-led sales
cast.secret: The investment committee meets next Tuesday and this is the last Series A slot for the quarter, so the data room is needed by Monday to stay in contention
cast.reveal_when: asks directly about their decision timeline or process for next steps
red_lines: will not offer network intros without a specific ask
will not extend past the hard stop
cast.history: He was introduced by the founder's accelerator mentor and grabbed coffee with him in SoMa two weeks ago to talk distribution through suppliers. His last exchange was advising him to focus today's pitch on the go-to-market wedge beyond independent cafes.

scenario.opening_line: Alright, welcome back — you were at $22k at the Showcase and I told you to bring real market math. You've got twenty minutes, you're at $35k MRR from cafes — so prove why this is a Series A company and not just a nice small business tool?
phases: Ask and close on next steps

events.description: Sarah checks her phone and says they now have only 10 minutes left and need to get to the numbers.
An associate knocks and hands Marcus a note: a direct competitor in cafe tech just announced a $12M raise this morning.

success_criteria: States a clear Series A ask and planned use of funds
Addresses retention and acquisition costs with specific numbers when pressed
Makes a venture-scale case beyond the current 120 cafes
Secures a concrete follow-up with owner, materials, and deadline
